# Mermaid Card

> A Home Assistant Lovelace card (`custom:mermaid-card`) that renders Mermaid diagrams. The diagram source is a Home Assistant template, so states, attributes, areas and floors can go into labels, branches, styles or the whole diagram; nodes and edges can be bound to entities. This file is for AI assistants writing such cards: what the card does with a config, the patterns that work, the traps, and tested examples.

Repository: https://github.com/timmaurice/lovelace-mermaid-card · Mermaid syntax: https://mermaid.js.org/intro/

## Config

```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
title: Heating            # optional card header
diagram_type: flowchart   # optional; used when content has no header line of its own
direction: LR             # optional; flowcharts only: TB (default), BT, LR, RL
scale: 100                # optional; percent of the natural size, 100 fits the card
content: |                # required; Mermaid source, may contain templates
  A[Heat pump] flow@--> B["Boiler<br>{{ states('sensor.boiler_temperature') }} °C"]
entities:                 # optional; node or edge id -> entity
  B: sensor.boiler_temperature
  flow: switch.heat_pump
  A:
    entity: switch.heat_pump
    tap_action: { action: toggle }
    hold_action: { action: more-info }
```

- `diagram_type` takes any Mermaid header keyword: `flowchart`, `sequenceDiagram`, `stateDiagram-v2`, `classDiagram`, `erDiagram`, `gantt`, `pie`, `mindmap`, `timeline`, `journey`, `sankey-beta`, `xychart-beta`, `kanban`, `quadrantChart`, `gitGraph`, `block-beta`, …
- Instead of `diagram_type`, `content` may start with its own header line (`flowchart LR`, `pie showData`). A header in the content wins. A header with extras (`pie showData`, `xychart-beta horizontal`) must be in the content: `diagram_type` holds only the keyword.
- Mermaid front matter (`---` / `config:` / `---`) may come first in `content`, before the header. Use it for per-diagram settings, e.g. `sankey: { showValues: true, linkColor: source }` or `xyChart: { width: 340, height: 320 }`.

## How a config becomes a diagram

1. If `content` contains `{{`, `{%` or a closed `{# … #}`, Home Assistant renders it as a template (websocket `render_template`, live). It re-renders when an entity the template reads changes, and every minute when it uses `now()`.
2. The rendered text gets a header from `diagram_type`/`direction` unless it has its own.
3. Mermaid draws it in strict security mode: no `click` callbacks or links, HTML in labels is sanitised.
4. The SVG is themed from the Home Assistant theme (light and dark), fitted to the card (shrinks to 75 %, then scrolls sideways; a button opens it full size).
5. Bindings in `entities` are applied to the drawn SVG, and again on every state change without redrawing.

## Bindings (`entities`)

- **Nodes** of flowcharts, state diagrams and class diagrams. The key is the node id (`HP` in `HP[Heat pump]`, the state name in a state diagram, the class name).
- **Gantt tasks and kanban items or columns**, by id: `wash` in `Wash :wash, 10:00, 2h`, `card1` in `card1[Clean filter]`. A Gantt task without an id cannot be bound reliably: give it one.
- **Mind map nodes, pie slices and sankey nodes**, by the text they show: `Kitchen` in `k[Kitchen]`, `Washer` in `"Washer" : 30`, `Solar` in `Solar,House,5`. A `<br>` counts as a space, markdown is read as its text. A label a template writes must be written identically as the key, so bind these only where the label is fixed or predictable. Pie slices and sankey nodes keep their chart colours and only take tap and hold; a bound slice's legend entry is tappable too.
- **Edges** of flowcharts. Name an edge with Mermaid's `@` syntax, `A e1@--> B`, and bind `e1`. Unnamed edges have ids like `L_A_B_0` (`L_<from>_<to>_<n>`).
- A value is an entity id, or a mapping with `entity`, `active_when`, `tap_action`, `hold_action` (Home Assistant's [action format](https://www.home-assistant.io/dashboards/actions/): `more-info`, `toggle`, `navigate`, `perform-action`, `url`, `none`).
- Node colour follows the entity's state: active (`on`, `open`, `heat`, `home`, any other text) gets the domain's active colour, inactive (`off`, `closed`, `idle`, `standby`, `not_home`, `locked`, `paused`, `docked`, `disarmed`) the inactive colour, `unavailable`/`unknown` the unavailable colour. Numeric states leave the node uncoloured: put values in the label instead. Gantt tasks, kanban items and mind map nodes take the colour too.
- Tap opens more-info unless `tap_action` says otherwise; a long press runs `hold_action` only when it is set. Edges take no actions. The *Controls* example below runs one of each action.
- A bound edge moves while its entity is active: on, open, heating, or a number other than zero. It takes the entity's colour, arrowhead included. How it moves comes from the diagram: `e1@{ animation: slow }` (or `fast`), or a `classDef` with its own `animation` applied with `class e1 …`; with none, it moves fast. "Reduce motion" stops all of it.
- `active_when: <state>` (or a list of states) makes only those states count as active, compared with the state as text. Several nodes can then share one entity and only the matching one lights up: active colour on a match, inactive colour otherwise, unavailable colour only when the entity is `unavailable`/`unknown`. On an edge it decides whether the edge moves. Quote numbers (`active_when: "3"`).

```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
diagram_type: stateDiagram-v2
content: |
  [*] --> Docked
  Docked --> Cleaning
  Cleaning --> Docked
entities:
  Docked: { entity: input_select.robot_vacuum, active_when: [Docked, Charging] }
  Cleaning: { entity: input_select.robot_vacuum, active_when: Cleaning }
```
- `speed: auto` on an edge binding moves it faster the higher the entity's value (absolute; a negative value moves backwards), from slow near zero to full speed at `max` (default 10000), by the square root of the value: a quarter of `max` moves half as fast. Set `max` to about the entity's peak, in the sensor's unit: `8000` for W, `8` for kW. Only the duration changes; the dash pattern stays the diagram's. `entities: { pv: { entity: sensor.solar_power, speed: auto, max: 8000 } }`

## Automation and its last run

`automation: automation.hall_light` in place of `content` draws that automation as a top-to-bottom flowchart (triggers, conditions, actions; `choose`/`if` as decisions, `repeat` as a loop) from its config, and marks the path of its latest trace: steps that ran get `classDef ran` (amber border), failed steps `classDef failed` (red), edges along the path animate. Labels come from each item's `alias`, else a short description. The top node (id `start`) is bound to the automation, so a tap opens its more-info. The card redraws when the automation runs. It needs an admin user (websocket `automation/config`, `trace/list`, `trace/get`) and an automation with an `id`. `parallel` and nested `sequence` blocks show as one step.

## Template patterns

- Value in a label: `T["Living room<br>{{ states('sensor.t', with_unit=True) }}"]`. Quote labels that contain anything but words: `["…"]`.
- State in words, translated: `{{ state_translated('sun.sun') }}`. Attributes: `{{ state_attr('climate.x', 'current_temperature') }}`.
- Choose a branch or a highlight: `{{ 'yes' if is_state('sun.sun', 'below_horizon') else 'no' }}@{ animation: slow }` and `class {{ 'A' if … else 'B' }} taken` with `classDef taken stroke-width:4px`.
- Build the diagram from the registry: `floors()`, `floor_name(f)`, `floor_areas(f)`, `areas()`, `area_name(a)`, `area_entities(a)`, `label_entities('x')`, `expand(...)`, `device_id(entity)`.
- Loop over states: `{% for e in states.input_boolean | selectattr('state', 'eq', 'on') %}…{% endfor %}`, `states | groupby('domain')`, `e.name`, `e.object_id`, `e.last_changed`, `e.attributes`.
- Times: `as_local(as_datetime(state_attr('sun.sun', 'next_setting'))).strftime('%H:%M')`, `relative_time(e.last_changed)`, `now()`. Put a repeated expression in a macro: `{% macro t(a) %}…{% endmacro %}`.
- Collect and sort: `{% set ns = namespace(items=[]) %}{% set ns.items = ns.items + [(key, label)] %}` then `ns.items | sort(attribute='0')`.
- Use `{%-` / `-%}` to keep template tags from leaving blank lines.
- Icons: Mermaid's icon shape takes Home Assistant icon names, `HP@{ icon: "mdi:heat-pump", label: "Heat pump" }`, also from a template: `icon: "{{ 'mdi:fan' if is_state('fan.x', 'on') else 'mdi:fan-off' }}"`. In `architecture-beta`: `service db(mdi:database)[Recorder]`, `group home(mdi:home)[Home]`. Prefixes: `mdi:` (every Material Design Icon), `hass:`, and those of custom icon integrations. Other Iconify sets (`logos:`, `fa:`) are not available; an unknown name shows a question mark.

## Traps

- **Home Assistant trims the rendered template**, so the first line loses its indentation. Where indentation is structure (mind map, kanban), write the top level at the start of the line and indent the rest relative to it.
- **Hexagons collide with templates:** `A{{text}}` is read as a template. Write `A{{ '{{' }}text{{ '}}' }}` or wrap the diagram in `{% raw %}…{% endraw %}`.
- **Colons separate fields** in Gantt tasks (`name :start, end`), timeline periods (`period : event`) and journey tasks (`task: score: actors`). Keep them out of names and periods: `| replace(':', ' ')`, or `strftime('%H.%M')` in a timeline period.
- **Parentheses and brackets are shapes:** a friendly name like `Lamp (hall)` in an unquoted node or mind map line starts a shape. Quote it in `["…"]` or `| replace('(', '')`.
- **Gantt `todayMarker`** uses the browser's clock and time zone; a `now()` milestone uses Home Assistant's. Use one, not both, when they can differ: `todayMarker off`.
- **Pie labels are quoted:** `"{{ domain }}" : {{ count }}`. `showData` goes on the header line: `pie showData` in the content, not `diagram_type`.
- **Wide diagram types** (sequence, pie with legend, sankey, timeline, journey, Gantt) need room: give them a wide card (two columns in a sections view) or `direction: TB` for flowcharts.
- Template errors show in the card as an alert; Mermaid parse errors too, and the visual editor shows them at the diagram field with the line number.

## Examples

Every example below renders as shown (tested against Home Assistant 2026.11 with Mermaid 12). Those on `sun.sun`, `zone.home`, `person`, `states` and the area and floor registry work in any installation. The others use demo helpers (`input_boolean.*`, `input_number.solar_power`, `input_number.*_temperature`, `input_select.robot_vacuum`): swap in your own entities.

### Flowchart
```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
title: Flowchart
content: |
  {%- set dark = is_state('sun.sun', 'below_horizon') %}
    SUN(["Sun<br>{{ state_translated('sun.sun') }}, {{ state_attr('sun.sun', 'elevation') | round(0) }}°"]) --> DARK{Dark outside?}
    DARK yes@-->|yes| SCENE["Evening scene<br>{{ state_translated('input_boolean.evening_scene') }}"]
    DARK no@-->|no| NOTHING[Nothing to do]
    {{ 'yes' if dark else 'no' }}@{ animation: slow }
    classDef taken stroke-width:4px
    class {{ 'SCENE' if dark else 'NOTHING' }} taken
entities:
  SCENE:
    entity: input_boolean.evening_scene
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
    hold_action:
      action: more-info
```

### Live flow
```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
title: Live flow
content: |
  HP["Heat pump<br>{{ states('input_boolean.heat_pump') }}"] power@--> BOIL[("Boiler")]
  BOIL circuit@--> FLOOR["Underfloor heating<br>{{ states('input_boolean.underfloor_heating') }}"]
  power@{ animation: fast }
  circuit@{ animation: slow }
entities:
  HP:
    entity: input_boolean.heat_pump
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
    hold_action:
      action: more-info
  power: input_boolean.heat_pump
  circuit: input_boolean.underfloor_heating
  FLOOR:
    entity: input_boolean.underfloor_heating
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
    hold_action:
      action: more-info
```

### State diagram
```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
title: State diagram
diagram_type: stateDiagram-v2
content: |
  [*] --> Docked
  Docked --> Cleaning: start
  Cleaning --> Returning: done
  Returning --> Docked
  Cleaning --> Error: stuck
  Error --> Docked: reset
  note right of {{ states('input_select.robot_vacuum') }}: now, since {{ relative_time(states.input_select.robot_vacuum.last_changed) }}
  classDef current stroke-width:4px,font-weight:bold
  class {{ states('input_select.robot_vacuum') }} current
```

### Controls
```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
title: Controls
direction: LR
content: |
  HOME(["Home"])
  HOME light@--> LIGHT["Kitchen light<br>{{ state_translated('input_boolean.kitchen_light') }}<br>tap: toggle"]
  HOME wash@--> WASH["Washer<br>{{ state_translated('input_boolean.washer') }}<br>tap: details · hold: toggle"]
  HOME --> TEMP["Living room<br>{{ states('input_number.living_room_temperature', with_unit=True) }}<br>tap: +0.5 · hold: back to 21"]
  HOME --> VAC["Robot vacuum<br>{{ states('input_select.robot_vacuum') }}<br>tap: next state"]
  HOME --> SOLAR["Solar<br>{{ states('input_number.solar_power') | int }} W<br>tap: energy dashboard"]
  HOME --> SUN["Sun<br>{{ state_translated('sun.sun') }}<br>tap: integration docs"]
entities:
  LIGHT:
    entity: input_boolean.kitchen_light
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
  light: input_boolean.kitchen_light
  WASH:
    entity: input_boolean.washer
    hold_action:
      action: toggle
  wash: input_boolean.washer
  TEMP:
    entity: input_number.living_room_temperature
    tap_action:
      action: perform-action
      perform_action: input_number.increment
      target:
        entity_id: input_number.living_room_temperature
    hold_action:
      action: perform-action
      perform_action: input_number.set_value
      target:
        entity_id: input_number.living_room_temperature
      data:
        value: 21
  VAC:
    entity: input_select.robot_vacuum
    tap_action:
      action: perform-action
      perform_action: input_select.select_next
      target:
        entity_id: input_select.robot_vacuum
    hold_action:
      action: more-info
  SOLAR:
    entity: input_number.solar_power
    tap_action:
      action: navigate
      navigation_path: "/energy"
  SUN:
    entity: sun.sun
    tap_action:
      action: url
      url_path: "https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sun/"
```

### Room temperatures
```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
title: Room temperatures
diagram_type: xychart-beta
content: |
  ---
  config:
    xyChart:
      width: 340
      height: 320
  ---
  {% set rooms = ['outdoor', 'living_room', 'kitchen', 'bedroom'] %}
    title "vs. 21 °C"
    x-axis [{% for r in rooms %}"{{ state_attr('input_number.' ~ r ~ '_temperature', 'friendly_name') | replace(' temperature', '') }}"{{ ', ' if not loop.last }}{% endfor %}]
    y-axis "°C" -10 --> 30
    bar [{% for r in rooms %}{{ states('input_number.' ~ r ~ '_temperature') | float(0) }}{{ ', ' if not loop.last }}{% endfor %}]
    line [21, 21, 21, 21]
```

### Energy flow
```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
title: Energy flow
diagram_type: sankey-beta
content: |
  ---
  config:
    sankey:
      showValues: true
      linkColor: source
  ---
  {% set solar = states('input_number.solar_power') | float(0) %}{% set home = states('input_number.home_consumption') | float(0) %}{% set pump = 900 if is_state('input_boolean.heat_pump', 'on') else 0 %}{% set wash = 500 if is_state('input_boolean.washer', 'on') else 0 %}
  {%- for source, target, value in [
    ('Solar', 'Home', [solar, home] | min),
    ('Solar', 'Grid export', [solar - home, 0] | max),
    ('Grid import', 'Home', [home - solar, 0] | max),
    ('Home', 'Heat pump', [pump, home] | min),
    ('Home', 'Washer', [wash, [home - pump, 0] | max] | min),
    ('Home', 'Everything else', [home - pump - wash, 0] | max),
  ] if value > 0 %}
  {{ source }},{{ target }},{{ value | round(0) }}
  {%- endfor %}
```

### Kanban
```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
title: Kanban
diagram_type: kanban
content: |
  {%- for column, state in [('On', 'on'), ('Off', 'off')] %}
  {{ state }}_column[{{ column }}]
  {%- for e in states.input_boolean | selectattr('state', 'eq', state) %}
    {{ e.object_id }}[{{ e.name }}]{% if area_name(e.entity_id) %}@{ assigned: '{{ area_name(e.entity_id) }}' }{% endif %}
  {%- endfor %}
  {%- endfor %}
```

### Pie chart
```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
title: Pie chart
content: |
  pie showData
    title Entities by domain
  {%- set ns = namespace(rows=[]) %}
  {%- for domain, items in states | groupby('domain') %}{% set ns.rows = ns.rows + [(items | count, domain)] %}{% endfor %}
  {%- set rows = ns.rows | sort(reverse=true) %}
  {%- for count, domain in rows[:6] %}
    "{{ domain }}" : {{ count }}
  {%- endfor %}
  {%- if rows | count > 6 %}
    "other" : {{ rows[6:] | map(attribute='0') | sum }}
  {%- endif %}
```

### Mind map
```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
title: Mind map
diagram_type: mindmap
content: |
  root(({{ state_attr('zone.home', 'friendly_name') or 'Home' }}))
  {%- for f in floors() %}
    {{ floor_name(f) }}
  {%- for a in floor_areas(f) %}
  {%- set temperature = area_entities(a) | select('match', 'input_number[.].*temperature') | first %}
      {{ area_name(a) }}{{ ' · ' ~ states(temperature, with_unit=True) if temperature }}
  {%- endfor %}
  {%- endfor %}
```

### Sequence diagram
```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
title: Sequence diagram
diagram_type: sequenceDiagram
content: |
  {%- macro t(a, f='%H:%M') %}{{ as_local(as_datetime(state_attr('sun.sun', a))).strftime(f) }}{% endmacro %}
  {%- set dark = is_state('sun.sun', 'below_horizon') %}
    autonumber
    participant Sun
    participant HA as Home Assistant
    participant Scene as Evening scene
    Sun->>HA: sets at {{ t('next_setting') }}, rises at {{ t('next_rising') }}
    Note over Sun,HA: elevation now {{ state_attr('sun.sun', 'elevation') | round(1) }}°
    alt {{ 'it is dark' if dark else 'still daylight' }}
      HA->>Scene: {{ 'turn on' if dark else 'wait until sunset' }}
      Scene-->>HA: {{ state_translated('input_boolean.evening_scene') }}
    end
    HA->>HA: {{ states.input_boolean | selectattr('state', 'eq', 'on') | list | count }} helpers on
```

### Class diagram
```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
title: Class diagram
diagram_type: classDiagram
content: |
  {%- for e in [states.sun.sun, states.zone.home, states.person | first] if e %}
    class {{ e.entity_id | replace('.', '_') }}["{{ e.name }}"] {
      +state {{ e.state }}
    {%- for k, v in e.attributes.items() if k not in ['friendly_name', 'icon', 'entity_picture', 'editable', 'id', 'user_id', 'device_trackers', 'passive', 'persons', 'radius'] and (v is number or v is string) %}
    {%- if loop.index <= 5 %}
      +{{ k }} {{ as_local(as_datetime(v)).strftime('%H:%M') if v is string and v is match('[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T') else v }}
    {%- endif %}
    {%- endfor %}
    }
  {%- endfor %}
    zone_home "1" --> "*" {{ (states.person | first).entity_id | replace('.', '_') }} : is home
    sun_sun ..> zone_home : shines on
entities:
  sun_sun: sun.sun
  zone_home: zone.home
```

### Entity relationship
```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
title: Entity relationship
diagram_type: erDiagram
content: |
  FLOOR ||--|{ AREA : contains
  AREA ||--o{ DEVICE : holds
  DEVICE ||--|{ ENTITY : provides
  AREA ||--o{ ENTITY : holds
  FLOOR {
    int count "{{ floors() | count }}"
  }
  AREA {
    int count "{{ areas() | count }}"
  }
  DEVICE {
    int count "{{ states | map(attribute='entity_id') | map('device_id') | reject('none') | unique | list | count }}"
  }
  ENTITY {
    int count "{{ states | count }}"
    int unavailable "{{ states | selectattr('state', 'in', ['unavailable', 'unknown']) | list | count }}"
  }
```

### Gantt chart
```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
title: Gantt chart
diagram_type: gantt
content: |
  {%- macro t(a, f='%H:%M') %}{{ as_local(as_datetime(state_attr('sun.sun', a))).strftime(f) }}{% endmacro %}
    dateFormat HH:mm
    axisFormat %H:%M
    todayMarker off
    section Sun
    Night :00:00, {{ t('next_dawn') }}
    Twilight :{{ t('next_dawn') }}, {{ t('next_rising') }}
    Daylight :active, {{ t('next_rising') }}, {{ t('next_setting') }}
    Twilight :{{ t('next_setting') }}, {{ t('next_dusk') }}
    Night :{{ t('next_dusk') }}, 23:59
    Now :milestone, {{ now().strftime('%H:%M') }}, 0m
    section Running
  {%- for e in states.input_boolean | selectattr('state', 'eq', 'on') %}
    {{ e.name | replace(':', ' ') }} :{{ as_local(e.last_changed).strftime('%H:%M') }}, {{ [1, ((now() - e.last_changed).total_seconds() / 60) | round(0, 'ceil') | int] | max }}m
  {%- endfor %}
```

### Timeline
```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
title: Timeline
diagram_type: timeline
content: |
  {%- macro t(a, f='%H:%M') %}{{ as_local(as_datetime(state_attr('sun.sun', a))).strftime(f) }}{% endmacro %}
  {%- set ns = namespace(items=[(now().strftime('%H.%M'), 'Now, sun at ' ~ (state_attr('sun.sun', 'elevation') | round(0)) ~ '°')]) %}
  {%- for a, label in [('next_dawn', 'Dawn'), ('next_rising', 'Sunrise'), ('next_noon', 'Noon'), ('next_setting', 'Sunset'), ('next_dusk', 'Dusk')] %}
  {%- set ns.items = ns.items + [(t(a, '%H.%M'), label)] %}
  {%- endfor %}
    title The sun today
  {%- for time, label in ns.items | sort(attribute='0') %}
    {{ time }} : {{ label }}
  {%- endfor %}
```

### User journey
```yaml
type: custom:mermaid-card
title: User journey
diagram_type: journey
content: |
  {%- macro comfort(entity) %}{{ [1, 5 - ((states(entity) | float(21) - 21) | abs | round(0) | int)] | max }}{% endmacro %}
  {%- set elevation = state_attr('sun.sun', 'elevation') | float(0) %}
    title A day at home
    section Morning
      Wake up at {{ states('input_number.bedroom_temperature') }} °C: {{ comfort('input_number.bedroom_temperature') }}: Bedroom
      Breakfast at {{ states('input_number.kitchen_temperature') }} °C: {{ comfort('input_number.kitchen_temperature') }}: Kitchen
    section Daytime
      Daylight, sun at {{ elevation | round(0) }}°: {{ 5 if elevation > 20 else 3 if elevation > 0 else 1 }}: Sun
      Robot vacuum {{ states('input_select.robot_vacuum') | lower }}: {{ 1 if is_state('input_select.robot_vacuum', 'Error') else 4 }}: Home Assistant
    section Evening
      Living room at {{ states('input_number.living_room_temperature') }} °C: {{ comfort('input_number.living_room_temperature') }}: Living room
      Evening scene {{ states('input_boolean.evening_scene') }}: {{ 5 if is_state('input_boolean.evening_scene', 'on') else 2 }}: Home Assistant
```
